java.assessment: The inline named-note form owns `note + whitespace + %g` and the multiline form owns `note as CODE`; both execute even when the resulting Display is empty. The multiline body comes from `BlocLines.subExtract(1, 1).removeEmptyColumns().toDisplay()`.
%g expands to U+0022, U+201C, U+201D and U+E121 everywhere, and %s includes NBSP in addition to ordinary whitespace.
Tag bodies exclude the full Pattern2 %g alphabet; fresh inline negative controls still reject in both products.
The Description command inventory registers named-note, note-on-link, and attached-note factories in the same family. Plain floating `note : ...` is not a valid Description command.
Attached-note commands remain valid after a completed named note; both fresh attached-note controls pass.
Java accepts `note on link : ...` after the preceding link and emits the link note in both single-line and multiline forms.
Java requires every source line to be consumed by a registered command and rejects unmatched candidates with syntax-error output.
Factory selection returns the first Description diagram factory that parses successfully and otherwise merges errors.

rust.assessment: The third follow-up keeps the repaired `%g` ownership model: fresh inline positive controls accept asymmetric delimiters and fresh `%g`-inside-DISPLAY/tag negatives still reject.

After a multiline note opener is accepted, the terminator path trims the accumulated body and emits no note when the trimmed body is empty. Component still also accepts plain floating notes through `RE_NOTE_MULTI_PLAIN`.

Deployment skips blank lines before checking whether a named-note accumulator is active, so blank body lines are lost. The family still has attached-note branches but no note-on-link branch after a completed named note.

causal_assessment.first_disproof: Component multiline named notes still diverge after successful recognition: `parse_component` trims the accumulated body on terminator and suppresses note creation when the body is empty or blank-only, while Java still creates the named note entity.
causal_assessment.second_disproof: Deployment multiline named notes still diverge after successful recognition: `parse_deployment` skips blank lines before the `note_accum` branch, so valid blank body lines vanish from the note text even though Java preserves them as NBSP spacer lines in the rendered note.
causal_assessment.third_disproof: The Description-family ownership boundary remains incomplete after a completed named note. Deployment still drops a valid `note on link : ...` command, and a component-shaped source with a completed named note followed by plain `note : ...` falls into Rust Class parsing even though Java returns a syntax error.

findings.title: Component still drops valid empty or blank-only multiline named notes after successful recognition
findings.java_provenance: CommandFactoryNote.createMultiLine always executes `executeInternal` after `subExtract(1, 1)` and does not reject an empty Display; Java SVGs for `component_multiline_empty_body_relation` and `component_multiline_blank_only_nested_relation` both contain named note entities.
findings.rust_data_flow: `parse_component` joins the accumulated body, trims it, and only pushes a note when the trimmed text is non-empty ([component.rs] lines 374-390). The opener was already accepted at lines 798-812, so Rust returns success with no note object.
findings.impact: Fresh valid Java notes disappear in Rust while later connections still target the missing note codes.

findings.title: Deployment still strips valid blank body lines from multiline named notes
findings.java_provenance: Java `CommandMultilines2` keeps the body lines inside the accepted multiline command, and the rendered note contains an ` ` spacer line for both blank-line probes.
findings.rust_data_flow: `parse_deployment` skips every blank trimmed line before it checks `note_accum` ([deployment.rs] lines 566-570), so blank and NBSP-only body lines never reach the accumulator. The terminator path then joins only the surviving nonblank lines ([deployment.rs] lines 589-607).
findings.impact: Fresh valid Deployment notes lose body structure even though the note itself is otherwise accepted.

findings.title: Deployment still omits a valid note-on-link command after a completed named note
findings.java_provenance: DescriptionDiagramFactory registers `CommandFactoryNoteOnLink`, and the Java SVG for `deployment_multiline_then_note_on_link` contains the link-note text `deployment link note should survive`.
findings.rust_data_flow: After named-note and attached-note handling, `parse_deployment` has no note-on-link branch before it moves on to node and connection parsing ([deployment.rs] lines 774-820). The forced Deployment YAML therefore contains only the named note `ForceDeployLink` and no link note.
findings.impact: A valid Java control following a completed named note still vanishes in the frozen Rust product.

findings.title: A component-shaped plain floating-note boundary still succeeds under the wrong Rust family
findings.java_provenance: Plain floating `note : ...` is not registered as a valid Description command in Java, so `component_multiline_then_plain_floating_note` returns a syntax-error SVG.
findings.rust_data_flow: The frozen Rust product succeeds on the same source by selecting the Class parser and materializing `note` as an ordinary class with a field, while also retaining the previously completed named note. The resulting YAML has `type: Class` rather than a Component-family diagram.
findings.impact: This remains an executable command-inventory and factory-selection mismatch at the boundary around completed named-note syntax.

findings.title: The third follow-up keeps the earlier `%g` repairs intact on fresh inline probes
findings.detail: Fresh asymmetric-delimiter positives pass in both Component and Deployment, and fresh embedded-DISPLAY and tag-body `%g` negatives still reject before later relation mutation.

findings.title: Attached-note and Component note-on-link controls still work after completed named notes
findings.detail: Fresh Component attached-note and note-on-link controls, plus a fresh Deployment attached-note control, all survive in the frozen product.

anti_overfit_audit.evidence: Searches of shipping crates found no mechanism name, followup3 case names, perturbation paths, or held-out labels. The only `include_str!` matches are pre-existing theme assets and the renderer oracle self-source table, not this mechanism's fixtures.

residue_assessment: Java versus Rust error-page SVG artwork, diagnostics, and line-number wording were not compared; acceptance, preserved SVG structure, and Rust YAML semantics were the oracle.

The deployment link-note mismatch was previously declared as a separate defect, but the prompt explicitly required challenging note-on-link ownership after completed named notes; the preserved case remains a valid Java-versus-Rust mismatch.

The component plain floating-note case is broader than the core terminal-rejection claim, but it directly exercises the requested plain-note and factory-selection boundary after a completed named note and remains executable.
verdict_reason: REJECT. The third follow-up keeps the earlier `%g` ownership fixes intact, but it still fails six fresh executable probes: two Component cases where valid empty or blank-only multiline named notes disappear, two Deployment cases where valid blank body lines are stripped, one forced-Deployment case where a valid `note on link` still vanishes, and one component-shaped source where Java reports syntax error while Rust succeeds under the wrong parser family. The frozen Rust binary hash stayed ad2e5a4bc2a1e7164ed3566c4ccce69635f79aa5afb2bb276c4657776ddaddf5 before and after.
